title: Chest Tube Output Trend
scenario: A 40-year-old female client has a chest tube placed after a thoracotomy. The nurse records chest tube drainage hourly to monitor for hemorrhage.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Reviewing the chest tube flowsheet, which action should the nurse take first?

options.text: Notify the surgeon immediately of the increasing bloody output
Continue routine monitoring and reassess in one hour
Clamp the chest tube to slow the drainage
Strip the chest tube vigorously to clear clots

questions.rationale: Drainage exceeding 100 mL/hr that is increasing and turning bright red, with rising heart rate and falling blood pressure, signals active hemorrhage and requires immediate provider notification. Clamping or vigorous stripping is unsafe.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: For each finding in the trend, click to specify whether it is expected or a cause for concern.

rows.text: Serosanguineous drainage of 60 mL in the first hour
Drainage rising to 220 mL in one hour
Tidaling present with no air leak

questions.rationale: Modest serosanguineous output and tidaling without an air leak are expected early after thoracotomy. Rapidly rising, bright-red drainage with a falling blood pressure indicates hemorrhage and is a concern.
